title: Operational safeguards and procedures: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel
author: Asha Patel
body:
Purpose

This document consolidates company-wide operational safeguards and standard procedures for access & permissions, change management, data classification and retention, procurement & expenses, vendor lifecycle, travel policy, and the canonical internal templates. It is intended as a single reference for approvers, system owners, and people managers responsible for compliance and day-to-day operations.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and approved vendors interacting with corporate systems, customer data, procurement systems, and travel bookings.
- Excludes standalone research experiments that do not touch production systems or customer data unless otherwise noted.

Owner and escalation

- Primary owner: Finance & Legal (owner_team).
- Secondary owners: Security (for RBAC and data classification), People Ops (for travel & expense policy), Eng Platform (for change management tooling).
- Escalation path: Document owner -> Security Lead -> Head of Finance -> General Counsel.

1) Access and permissions (RBAC and least privilege)

Overview

Redwood uses an RBAC-first model enforced by Okta (SSO) and 1Password/Secrets Manager for credential access. Access to production systems requires an approved justification, manager sign-off, and an owner-level attestation every 180 days.

Access tiers

- Tier 0 (Privileged production ops): access to production control plane (Redwood-ops, Kubernetes cluster admin) — approval required from Eng SRE and Security, quarterly audit.
- Tier 1 (Engineering production access): model serving consoles, logs, trace links — manager approval + security training.
- Tier 2 (Internal tools): billing dashboards, analytics, internal docs. Manager approval.
- Tier 3 (General access): corporate email, Slack, HR systems. Auto-provisioned on hire.

Provisioning workflow (high level)

1. Request initiated in AccessFlow (self-service portal) with justification and duration.
2. Manager approval within 3 business days.
3. Security vet for Tier 0/Tier 1 within 2 business days.
4. Provisioning executed by Identity team using Okta SCIM and Terraform modules (audit log generated).
5. Request recorded in access ledger (internal Confluence page and SysAudit).

Periodic reviews and attestations

- Owners must run quarterly access reviews for resources they own.
- Managers must attest to the continued need for any Tier 0/1 access every 180 days. Non-attested access will be revoked after a 14-day grace notification.

Emergency access

- Temporary emergency elevation is granted via the PagerDuty emergency workflow and must be logged within 24 hours in the Emergency Access Log with justification and post-facto approval by Security.

2) Change management and deployment controls

Principles

- Make changes small, reversible, and observable.
- Enforce canary/circuit-breaker patterns for runtime changes affecting customer traffic.

Change categories and approval levels

- Routine (low risk): documentation, non-production config changes — auto-approve with CI pipeline checks.
- Standard (medium risk): infra as code updates, non-customer-facing runtime config — owner review + SRE sign-off.
- High risk: production schema migrations, model version rollouts that affect >5% traffic, network changes — change advisory board (CAB) approval required.
- Emergency: production-severity incidents remediated outside normal change windows; post-mortem required and CAB retro review.

Release windows and SLOs

- Default production deployment window: 09:00–17:00 PT weekdays.
- SLOs for deployment success: 99% of automated canary checks must pass before rollout continues.
- If canary failures exceed 5% requests with errors, automatic rollback triggers.

Change request template (short)

- Title, owner, services impacted, risk level, rollback plan, monitoring/alerts, test checklist, CAB approvers.

3) Data classification and retention

Classification levels

- PUBLIC: information safe for the public internet.
- INTERNAL: company information intended for employees and contractors (default).
- RESTRICTED: business-critical or customer-provided data requiring encryption at rest and in transit; access limited to Tier 1+.
- SENSITIVE_PII: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) regulated by GDPR/CCPA; extra controls and data minimization required.

Retention and deletion policy (examples)

- Logs (infra-level): retained 90 days in hot storage, 365 days in cold storage (audit index).
- Product analytics: aggregated data retained 2 years; raw event traces retained 90 days.
- Customer contractual data: retention per contract; default 7 years unless shorter period requested.
- Employee PII: retained as required by law; HR to coordinate deletion requests.

Data handling controls

- All RESTRICTED and SENSITIVE_PII must be stored in approved encrypted stores (GCP Cloud Storage with CMEK or equivalent) and access governed by IAM roles.
- No production secrets may be copied to developer laptops. Developer sandbox data must be anonymized or synthetic.

Data incident reporting

- Any suspected data exposure must be reported to Security within 4 hours. Security will lead triage and notify Legal for any customer or regulator notification obligations.

4) Procurement, vendor onboarding, and expenses

Procurement roles and tools

- Systems: ProcureFlow (purchase requests & approvals), Workday (invoicing & expense reimbursement), and VendorHub (vendor metadata & contracts registry).
- Approvers: Manager (up to $5k), Department Head (>$5k–$50k), Finance Director (>$50k). Legal signs off on contracts >$25k or any agreement with data processing implications.

Vendor onboarding checklist

1. Business justification and scope of work.
2. Risk assessment using VendorHub template (security, privacy, continuity).
3. Contract review by Legal (use CLA/standard SOW where applicable).
4. Security questionnaire for vendors with RESTRICTED data access; SOC2 or equivalent required when applicable.
5. Finance PO created in ProcureFlow; Finance Director approves for spend >$50k.
6. Vendor added to VendorHub and scheduled for annual review.

Approval SLA and timing expectations

- Routine hardware/software purchases: 5–7 business days.
- New vendor onboarding with legal/security review: 10–21 business days depending on complexity.

Expense policy summary (travel & non-travel)

- Reimbursement platform: Workday Expenses. Receipts required for >$25.
- Approval chain: direct manager -> finance review (for cross-team budget).
- Per diem: domestic $75/day, international $125/day unless conference rate applies.
- Mileage: $0.66/mile (US standard).
- Corporate card: issued on manager & Finance approval; monthly reconciliation required.

5) Vendor lifecycle and third-party risk management

Risk tiers and controls

- Low risk: SaaS productivity tools with no customer data — onboarding via standard PO and basic review.
- Medium risk: tools with aggregated analytics or limited customer metadata — require a security questionnaire and approval by Security.
- High risk: vendors processing customer data or ML model providers with model/key access — require SOC2, contract data processing agreement (DPA), technical controls (VPC peering, private endpoints), and quarterly security review.

Ongoing monitoring

- Annual vendor review for medium/high risk.
- Quarterly billing and usage review for vendors with committed spend >$10k/month.
- Automated alerts from VendorHub for contract renewals 90/30/7 days out.

Termination checklist

1. Confirm contractual termination clauses and notice windows.
2. Revoke all vendor credentials and network access within 48 hours of termination effective date.
3. Verify data return or deletion per contract within contract-defined window; log verification in VendorHub.

6) Travel policy (high level)

Booking and approval

- All business travel must be requested via TravelPortal and pre-approved by manager. Non pre-approved travel may be denied reimbursement except in emergencies.
- Preferred booking vendors: Redwood Travel Partner (consolidated itineraries for compliance and refunds).

Class limits and exceptions

- Domestic coach economy for flights <6 hours. Premium economy or business permitted with VP approval.
- Hotel: standard business class; managers can approve upgrades for late arrivals or safety reasons.

Safety and COVID-era guidance

- Employees must follow local travel advisories and Redwood security travel advisories. For high-risk geographies, travel requires VP-level approval and security briefing.

Expense reconciliation

- Submit expenses with receipts in Workday within 14 days of trip completion. Finance will audit 5% of travel claims monthly.

7) Templates and supporting artifacts

Canonical templates (links and short description)

- expense-claim-template.xlsx: standardized expense categories and example receipts mapping.
- vendor-risk-assessment-template.docx: checklist used during onboarding to score risk.
- change-request-template.md: short-form CR with rollback and monitoring checklist.
- access-request-form: Okta-backed form auto-posted to AccessFlow.
- data-classification-matrix.csv: mapping of systems to classification level and retention.

How to use templates

- Templates live in /confluence/templates/operational-templates and are the single source of truth. Fill templates electronically and attach to ProcureFlow or change ticket.

8) Governance, metrics, and continuous improvement

Key metrics to track (examples)

- Time-to-approve for access requests (target: median <= 2 business days).
- Percentage of Tier 0 access with current attestation (target: 100%).
- Mean time-to-onboard vendor (target: <= 15 business days).
- Percentage of changes with automated canary checks (target: 95%).

Audit and reporting cadence

- Quarterly cross-functional governance review (Finance, Security, People Ops, Eng Platform).
- Annual compliance audit for data handling and vendor risk.

Appendix A — Quick checklists

A1. New employee provisioning checklist

1. Create HR record and send offer packet.
2. Provision directory account (Okta) and corporate email.
3. Add to Slack and team groups.
4. Assign baseline Tier 3 permissions.
5. Schedule security onboarding training within 5 business days.

A2. Quick procurement checklist (<= $5k)

1. Submit ProcureFlow request with justification.
2. Manager approves.
3. Finance issues PO and vendor paid.

Contacts and escalation list

- Procurement & Expenses: finance-ops@redwood.com
- Vendor onboarding: vendorops@redwood.com
- Access & Identity: identity@redwood.com
- Security incident reporting: sec-incident@redwood.com (pager: +1-555-0102 treat as 24/7)
